🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico at the UN: We Reject the Committee's Reading of Article 34</u>

At the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, Interior Ministry undersecretary Arturo Medina Padilla rejected the Committee on Enforced Disappearances' interpretation of Article 34, the clause it activated against Mexico in March. The committee itself found no evidence of a federal policy of disappearances. Medina Padilla cited more than 16,000 people located in 2026, a review of the national registry alongside the UN human rights office, and forensic cooperation with Germany, Spain, Norway, Canada and Guatemala. "Our commitment is clear: find the disappeared, fight impunity and guarantee the rights of families."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS Raises Its Pay Offer to 8% and Makes 10,939 Jobs Permanent</u>

IMSS's Technical Council approved an 8% raise for its workers, up from the 6.8% offer they rejected in the wage consultation. Director Zoé Robledo said 4% goes straight into base salary and 4% into housing assistance. The package also gives permanent positions to 10,939 workers, including staff hired during Covid, plus more medicine, equipment and hospital maintenance. Sheinbaum had said the money would come from cutting administrative spending.

🇲🇽💧 <u>Federal Money for Guadalajara's Clean Water: Up to 13 Billion Pesos</u>

President Sheinbaum announced that the federal government will fund a water treatment plant for metropolitan Guadalajara. Conagua director Efraín Morales puts the cost at 12 to 13 billion pesos. Jalisco is already building its own plant worth about 7.5 billion. Federal and state teams meet today to settle the financing, with the goal of doing it without new debt. Ten days ago, thousands marched in Guadalajara over dirty tap water.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Hacienda Pushes 238 Billion Pesos of Debt Out to 2047</u>

Mexico's Finance Ministry refinanced 238.153 billion pesos of domestic debt, swapping Cetes, Bondes F, Bonos M and Udibonos maturing between 2026 and 2043 for paper running to 2047 and stretching the average maturity by 2.9 years, El Economista reports. 123.9 billion of it was due in 2027. It is the sixth operation of the year: debt service came in 121.9 billion pesos under budget in January-August, and the broadest measure of public debt sits at 51.5% of GDP, mostly in pesos at fixed rates.

🇲🇽🏳️‍🌈 <u>Querétaro's PAN Government Blocks the Gender Identity Law a Second Time</u>

Querétaro's Congress passed a Gender Identity Law with 15 votes, and Governor Mauricio Kuri's administration sent it back again. Morena's state coordinator Santiago Nieto and the Morena caucus say the September 22 observations are wording and spelling notes, not legal objections, and that the law only covers administrative procedures for adults. Activists say Querétaro is among the last eight states still denying this right. "It is incredible that we are still a conservative island in the middle of a progressive and liberal country," Nieto said. Morena is now weighing the fastest legal route to force its publication.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>National Guard Plugs Into Mexico's Central Intelligence Platform</u>

Defense Secretary Ricardo Trevilla and Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch signed an agreement connecting the National Guard's systems to the Central Intelligence Platform run by the CNI, with real-time consultation of each other's records to map criminal networks. A joint CNI-GN group will meet quarterly, and every investigation that comes out of it stays under the command of the public prosecutor. "No institution can carry out this task in isolation," Harfuch said.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum to the INE: Explain Those Contracts</u>

Asked by Contralínea at the mañanera, Sheinbaum said Mexico's electoral institute must clarify the alleged corruption in its procurement and "give all the information and transparency." Open FGR, SAT and UIF files point to rigged contracts for electoral paper and supplies with firms such as Cajas Graf, Formas Finas y Materiales and Corporativo Zeg, and to suspected laundering, embezzlement and shell companies. Those under investigation include Jesús Octavio García González, INE's executive director of administration until April 2026, and a former director from Lorenzo Córdova's tenure. The Federal Audit Office could step in, she said, "because these are public resources, resources of the people of Mexico."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS Pay Offer Coming This Week, Funded by Cutting Bureaucracy</u>

Sheinbaum said IMSS director Zoé Robledo will present a salary proposal for the institute's workers this week, paid for by cutting administrative spending without touching medical services. Workers had rejected a 6.8% offer in this month's consultation. On Tuesday, rank-and-file IMSS staff delivered their demands to the Presidency: a 10% direct raise, more staff, equipment and medicine, and health spending of at least 7% of GDP.

🇲🇽💳 <u>Senate Passes Digital Payments Law, 73 to 34</u>

Mexico's Senate approved the Digital Economy Law on Tuesday and sent it to President Sheinbaum for publication. Federal, state and municipal governments will have to accept digital payments for every procedure and service, the Digital CURP can be used to open financial services remotely, and Hacienda gets 15 working days after the decree takes effect to name the sectors where electronic payment becomes mandatory. PAN, PRI and MC voted against giving Hacienda that power. The Chamber of Deputies passed it on October 6.

🇲🇽📈 <u>INEGI: Economy Up 3.7% Year on Year in September</u>

INEGI's Timely Indicator estimates that Mexico's economic activity grew 3.7% from a year earlier in September, with services up 4% and industry up 3.6%. Month on month it rose only 0.1%, after an estimated 0.5% in August, so El Economista calls it a slowdown. Still, Monex expects activity to have kept expanding through the whole third quarter. Economy Secretary Ebrard says the latest numbers justify revising growth forecasts upward.
